description: How Domino's turned clicks into dominance — and how the rest of fast food scrambled to keep up (2006–2026). This chart race traces the percent of U.S. sales generated via digital channels (mobile app, online ordering, third-party delivery) for four major chains. Real milestones: Domino’s digital-first overhaul and 2019–2021 dominance, Chipotle’s massive 2020 digital spike, Starbucks’ app/loyalty-driven growth, and McDonald’s steady ramp with delivery and self-service kiosks.
youtube_description:
The Digital Drive-Thru — how Domino’s rewired fast food and left the rest racing to catch up.

In this visualization we track the percentage of U.S. sales coming from digital channels (mobile app, website, delivery platforms) for Domino’s, Starbucks, McDonald’s and Chipotle from 2006 through 2026. Domino’s transformation (digital ordering, in‑house delivery integration, robust app and loyalty upgrades) produced a decade-long surge and a pandemic-era rocket to over two-thirds of U.S. sales by 2019–2020. Chipotle’s digital rebuild and order-ahead model caused a huge spike in 2020. Starbucks’ loyalty and mobile app fueled steady growth. McDonald’s leaned on kiosks and delivery partnerships to climb steadily.

Sources & notes: company annual reports and investor presentations (Domino’s investor facts, Starbucks annual reports, McDonald’s Form 10‑Ks, Chipotle investor releases), industry reports on digital sales penetration and delivery share. Specific milestone references: Domino’s reporting that digital made up ~65% of U.S. sales by late 2019, Chipotle’s 2020/2021 digital surge documented in company filings, Starbucks’ disclosure of app/loyalty-driven sales growth during the pandemic, and McDonald’s published disclosures on delivery/kiosk/digital mix. The 2025–2026 points are conservative forward projections based on the companies’ latest disclosed trends and continued consumer behavior toward digital ordering.
